title: Vibrato, Dutre, Roy Palmer and Ory
summary: He compares Dutre's smooth jazz solos with Roy's rough style, and rates Roy over Ory.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yeah. But even then your vibrato sounds a little different to me.
I noticed something different in the Tin Roof Blues.
It didn't sound like, say, Bernie's is vibrato at all.
Now how did you produce your vibrato back in the early days?

Well, to be truthful about the vibrato, I didn't pay any attention to the vibrato. You see, we'll just take Dutre for instance. Dutre and Zoo Robin was smooth. There was no one who played them shelly parts. And as you've heard Dutre when he played the jazz solos, his was a bit different than Roy. Roy would take a pair or something, you know, and put it over the bellies and it was rough, you know, gut bucket I'd say. Yeah. Now Roy, I'd come to Ory again. Ory was rough too. Yeah. But between the two, Ory couldn't touch Roy. But Ory composed two, muscat rambling things like Ory's Creole trombone. He was Louis Hot Five, and things like that. And so, and out in California, I was on the air, you know, in that picture. And so Ory just, the people just put him in a different category than Roy.
He's a much slicker character. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

He's a pretty good businessman. Yeah, yeah, but Roy was the best trombone player ever left here. Now there's one fellow way years ago I heard, see I used to sit on the stand with Joe, Oliver and his band, and him talking about these different bands, and there was one trombonist that his name was Baptiste Delaney, and he said he was the best he ever heard. But this is what's supposed to happen to Baptiste. He lost his mind, and he used to climb the lamppost, you know, with his trombone. And of course a lot of people don't believe in this, but they claim that this house where he lived, when he decided to tear this house down, or wreck it, they said he found between that mortar and stuff, his long underwear, stretch, an arm there, an arm there, and the legs, here and like that. And as soon as he tore that house down he regained his senses. But they say he was the best that they ever heard. That included all of them. But Roy was a good musician. Roy could read, Roy could play more than one instrument, you know. And he'd better read, a better musician than ever.
